reasoning.title: Commit-scope match
reasoning.description: Applies when counting commits for named contributors on a specified date in a GitLab project; not when the requested total is already supplied by a trustworthy project-wide report.
reasoning.content: Before answering, confirm every counted row visibly belongs to the requested project and relevant branch scope, displays the requested date, and identifies one of the requested contributors as the commit author.

reasoning.title: Complete date coverage
reasoning.description: Applies when the qualifying commits may be outside the initially loaded results, hidden by pagination, lazy loading, or date grouping; not when the interface explicitly proves the filtered result set is complete.
reasoning.content: Before answering, confirm you counted every qualifying commit across the full relevant history, including all pages or loaded sections, and that the displayed total equals the sum of the qualifying rows rather than an estimate from the first screen. If your current view cannot show that, one place that can is the project's commit-history view.

reasoning.title: Complete date-group count
reasoning.description: Applies when counting commits by author on a particular date, especially when the history is grouped by date or can continue beyond the visible screen. Not applicable when GitLab provides a verified aggregate for the exact author-and-date criteria.
reasoning.content: Before answering, confirm the target date heading and qualifying author names are visibly evidenced, every commit row in that date group has been inspected across scrolling, loading, or pagination boundaries, and the reported total equals the number of matching rows.

reasoning.title: Repository and branch scope
reasoning.description: Applies whenever a commit count could vary by project, fork, or selected branch. Not applicable when the task explicitly requests a site-wide count independent of repository and branch.
reasoning.content: Before answering, confirm the displayed project identity is the requested repository and the selected branch matches the requested scope, or the repository’s intended default branch when no branch is specified.

reasoning.title: Best-project claim is visibly supported
reasoning.description: Applies when “best” is interpreted using a measurable project attribute such as stars and the result must also meet language or implementation criteria; not when the user names a specific repository.
reasoning.content: Before answering, confirm the selected project qualifies as the requested implementation and has the highest visible star count among every qualifying project across the complete result set, including all result pages.

reasoning.title: SSH command matches the selected project
reasoning.description: Applies when returning an SSH clone command; not when the user requests another clone protocol.
reasoning.content: Before answering, confirm the complete command is visibly displayed as the SSH clone value for the selected project and matches that project’s namespace and repository, rather than being inferred from the page URL. If your current view cannot show that, one place that can is the project’s Clone menu.

reasoning.title: Complete, visibly verified clone command
reasoning.description: Applies when the user requests a runnable clone command rather than only a repository address; not when they explicitly request the URL alone.
reasoning.content: Before answering, confirm the answer includes `git clone` followed by the complete SSH URL exactly as visibly displayed for the selected project, with no portion inferred from the project path.

reasoning.title: Verified highest-starred matching project
reasoning.description: Applies when the requested repository must be selected by star ranking from matching GitLab projects; not when the user identifies one specific project directly.
reasoning.content: Before answering, confirm the selected project genuinely matches the requested tracker and has the highest visible star count across every qualifying result and any additional result pages, with both the project identity and ranking supported by recorded page text.

reasoning.title: Exhaustive commit count
reasoning.description: Applies when counting commits for a person within a date range and repository/ref scope; not when the task asks only about commits currently visible on one page.
reasoning.content: Before answering, confirm the total includes every qualifying commit across all result pages, with each commit inside the requested date range and repository/branch scope, rather than only the visible chronological segment.

reasoning.title: Successful evidence source
reasoning.description: Applies when a filter, API request, or alternate data source fails or returns an error; not when the complete result set was successfully retrieved and verified.
reasoning.content: Before answering, confirm the stated count is supported by a successfully loaded result set and that no failed request, missing project, or unpopulated author filter was treated as evidence that additional commits do not exist.

reasoning.title: Complete interval coverage
reasoning.description: Applies when counting commits across a date range, especially where the history is paginated, lazy-loaded, or truncated. Does not apply when the complete filtered result set is explicitly shown in one view.
reasoning.content: Before answering, confirm the count includes every qualifying commit row across the full requested interval and all result pages, with both date boundaries evidenced rather than inferred from a partially visible history.

reasoning.title: Correct author and repository scope
reasoning.description: Applies when an author name may be ambiguous or when repository, branch, or host assumptions could change the result. Does not apply when the task and displayed history uniquely establish all of these.
reasoning.content: Before answering, confirm every counted row shows the intended author and belongs to the displayed project and requested branch, and that evidence from another host or endpoint was not treated as equivalent after a project-not-found response.

reasoning.title: Contributor and repository scope
reasoning.description: Applies when counting commits for a named person in a specific GitLab project, branch, and time period, especially when names, usernames, or email identities may differ. Not needed when the task explicitly requests an unscoped repository-wide total for all contributors.
reasoning.content: Before answering, confirm every counted commit belongs to the requested project and branch and matches the intended contributor’s verified commit identity rather than merely a similar display name.

reasoning.title: Complete filtered count
reasoning.description: Applies whenever commit results may span pagination, lazy-loaded sections, multiple date groups, or an API response limit. Not needed when the result explicitly reports a trustworthy aggregate for the complete filtered interval.
reasoning.content: Before answering, confirm the count covers every qualifying commit across the full requested date interval and all result pages, not just the first visible screen or response page, and that both date boundaries were applied correctly.

reasoning.title: Exact project identity
reasoning.description: Applies when similarly named repositories, mirrors, forks, or multiple GitLab instances may exist; not needed when the project page visibly confirms the full namespace and repository name.
reasoning.content: Before answering, confirm the evidence comes from the project whose displayed namespace and repository name exactly match the requested project, rather than from a fork, mirror, search mention, or similarly named repository.

reasoning.title: Complete commit leaderboard
reasoning.description: Applies when identifying the leading contributor by commit count; not when the task asks about a different contribution measure such as merge requests, issues, or additions.
reasoning.content: Before answering, confirm the named person has the highest displayed commit total across the complete contributor set for the intended repository scope and branch/history, and that the ranking is based on commits rather than another activity metric.

reasoning.title: Contributor-level maximum
reasoning.description: Applies when the answer requires the person with the highest commit count; not when only repository-wide aggregate activity is requested.
reasoning.content: Before answering, confirm the named contributor has a visible contributor-specific commit total that is at least as high as every other contributor total, including any ties, rather than inferring the result from aggregate repository statistics. If your current view cannot show that, one place that can is the repository contributor graph.

reasoning.title: Complete contributor ranking
reasoning.description: Applies when contributors must be ranked by commits within a repository or branch; not when the task names contributors directly or asks only for aggregate activity.
reasoning.content: Before answering, confirm the reported contributors occupy the highest requested ranks by commit count across the complete contributor list, including all loaded sections or pages, and that the ranking is scoped to the exact repository and intended branch rather than inferred from aggregate charts.

reasoning.title: Contributor-email identity match
reasoning.description: Applies when contact details must be retrieved for contributors identified through repository activity; not when only names or commit totals are requested.
reasoning.content: Before answering, confirm every email is the complete author email displayed in commit metadata for the corresponding ranked contributor in the same repository, not an inferred address, profile label, username, unrelated committer address, or truncated value.

reasoning.title: Visible contributor evidence
reasoning.description: Applies when reporting contributor names and commit totals from a repository ranking; not when the user provides the values directly for transformation.
reasoning.content: Before answering, confirm every reported contributor name and commit count is visibly displayed in the contributor entries for the intended repository and branch, rather than inferred from narration or aggregate charts. If your current view cannot show that, one place that can is the repository’s Contributors view.

reasoning.title: Requested rank cutoff
reasoning.description: Applies when the requested number of ranked results intersects a tie; not when all ranks have distinct values or the user explicitly requests every tied entry.
reasoning.content: Before answering, confirm the response contains exactly the requested number of contributors, or clearly explains that additional names are included because of a tie at the cutoff and states the tie-handling convention.

reasoning.title: Complete access roster
reasoning.description: Applies when asked for everyone or everyone else with access to a GitLab project; not when the request names a particular member.
reasoning.content: Before answering, confirm every qualifying member row in the correct project’s access list was inspected across all sections, pagination, and dynamically loaded results, including directly added and inherited members where displayed.

reasoning.title: Grounded complete usernames
reasoning.description: Applies when the answer requires GitLab usernames rather than display names, and especially when the requester must be excluded; not when only names or aggregate counts are requested.
reasoning.content: Before answering, confirm each reported username is copied in full from visible username text in that member’s row, belongs to a user other than the signed-in requester, and is not inferred from a display name, avatar, or unrelated page text.

reasoning.title: Branch-scoped contributor maximum
reasoning.description: Applies when identifying the leading contributor on a particular repository branch, especially when history is paginated or lazy-loaded and author-name variants may appear. It does not apply when the task already supplies a verified contributor identity.
reasoning.content: Before answering, confirm the named contributor has the highest explicitly established commit count across every contributor in the exact repository branch, after traversing all pages or loaded history, accounting for ties, and merging name variants only when visible evidence shows they are the same identity. If your current view cannot show that, one place that can is the branch-scoped Contributors view or complete commit history.

reasoning.title: Email provenance and completeness
reasoning.description: Applies when the requested email must be derived from a contributor’s commit identity. It does not apply when only a public profile address is explicitly requested.
reasoning.content: Before answering, confirm the answer contains the complete visible author email from a commit belonging to the verified top contributor in the same repository branch, rather than a profile link, truncated value, unrelated contributor’s address, or committer email. If your current view cannot show that, one place that can is the commit’s full metadata or raw patch.

reasoning.title: Requested branch verified
reasoning.description: Applies when the requested branch differs from the currently displayed or default branch, especially before declaring the task infeasible. Does not apply when the page visibly identifies the requested branch as the active scope.
reasoning.content: Before answering, confirm the requested branch’s existence or absence from visible branch results, rather than inferring it from the default branch or an unshown search state. If your current view cannot show that, one place that can is the repository’s branch list.

reasoning.title: Top count scoped to branch
reasoning.description: Applies when reporting the largest contributor commit count for a particular branch. Does not apply to repository-wide totals or questions about a named contributor.
reasoning.content: Before answering, confirm the numeric count is the maximum among all contributors and that the contributors view visibly states it is counting commits to the requested branch, not the default or another branch.

reasoning.title: Requested branch is verified
reasoning.description: Applies whenever results must be scoped to a named branch, especially when that branch appears absent. Do not infer absence merely from a selector’s initial options or an unverified search result.
reasoning.content: Before answering, confirm the displayed branch scope exactly matches the requested branch name; if claiming the task is infeasible, confirm the complete, unfiltered branch list visibly excludes that exact name across all pages. If your current view cannot show that, one place that can is the All branches view.

reasoning.title: Top contributor and follower count match
reasoning.description: Applies when the answer requires finding the leading contributor by commits and then retrieving that person’s profile statistic. It does not apply when the task asks only for repository-wide totals.
reasoning.content: Before answering, confirm the identified contributor has the highest commit count across the complete contributor set for the verified branch, that the linked profile belongs to that same contributor, and that the answer contains the profile’s displayed follower count.
